lines.en: What makes the future so hard to predict is not that it is hidden, but that it has not decided yet.
It is said that the best way to predict the future is to invent it.
Were anyone in the year 1900 to describe today's world, it would have sounded like madness, not foresight.
However precise the forecast, the future retains the right to surprise us.
Not until a technology disappears into daily life do we stop calling it new.
It is likely that our grandchildren will find our fears as quaint as we find our grandparents'.
What the futurist gets wrong is not the direction of change, but its speed and its manners.
The report predicts, with admirable confidence, a world that its own authors admit may never exist.
Little is certain about the coming century, except that it will not resemble our plans for it.
Rarely has the future arrived on schedule; it tends to come early, late, or dressed as something else.
What the next decade demands of us is less prediction than preparation.
It is probable that the jobs of 2050 have not been named yet, just as 'app developer' had no name in 1990.
Were the future to send us one warning, it would probably arrive disguised as an inconvenience.
Not until the predictions of one generation are read by the next do we learn how innocent certainty sounds.
However advanced our tools become, the question they cannot answer is what we should want.
